findings.where: Screens 1, 9 and 12, the voltmeter model (V_FLAT 1.96, V_FULL 2.12)
findings.what: The example cell is full at 1.225 yet rests at 2.12 V full and 2.10 V at 90%, while the explain says weaker stationary acid rests lower (about 2.08 V full for 1.225 acid), so the screens teach a voltage-to-charge pairing the lesson itself calls wrong for this cell; lower the voltmeter line to suit 1.225 acid, or make the example cell a stronger-acid type, and keep 2.10 V = 90% only where it applies.

findings.where: Script constant NB (all value-and-unit text), seen on screen 1 at 360 px
findings.what: NB is a plain space, not a no-break space, so values split from their units on a phone: screen 1 ends a line on '2.10' and starts the next with 'V.'; set NB to '\u00a0'.
'The figures vary a little from guide to guide.' talks about the sources rather than the cell; say 'The exact figure varies with the cell.' or cut it.
Five footnotes, and [^4] (the liquid gets lighter) and [^5] (layered acid pushes the voltage up) sit on explanations, not on a rule or value he might look up; keep [^1], [^2] and [^3] only.
'So the reading is corrected to 25 °C' states one maker's reference as the rule, while makers use 20 °C or 25 °C; say 'Makers correct it to a set temperature, here 25 °C.'
